key_insight: Incorporating explicit structural priors into a diffusion-based generative model enables more faithful reconstruction of visual content from EEG and helps separate objective perceptual signals from subjective cognitive components.
problem_solved: Existing EEG-to-image methods focus on categorical or natural-image priors and fail to capture structural features or disentangle perception vs. cognition, limiting reconstruction fidelity and interpretability.
method: Encode EEG signals with a dedicated EEG encoder to produce conditioning latents for generation.

Integrate explicit structural information (e.g., edge/contour, spatial layout or segmentation cues) as guidance into a conditional diffusion decoder to steer image synthesis toward structure-consistent reconstructions.

Train jointly with objectives that encourage structure alignment and disentanglement between objective perceptual features and subjective cognitive signals (e.g., reconstruction + structure-consistency / contrastive losses).
impact: Provides a practical approach for more interpretable, structure-aware EEG-to-image reconstruction useful for neuroAI, BCI interfaces, and studies of visual cognition, improving fidelity and diagnostic value of decoded images.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: EEG input → EEG encoder → structural prior extractor → structure-guided diffusion decoder → reconstructed image

Ablation chart or bar plot: reconstruction quality (or qualitative fidelity) with/without structural guidance and with disentanglement losses
paper_title: Structure-Guided Diffusion Model for EEG-Based Visual Cognition Reconstruction
paper_authors: Yongxiang Lian, Yueyang Cang, Pingge Hu, Yuchen He, Li Shi
